content.text:
Gear items are written to Supabase in two ways:

## 1. **Single gear item addition** (`handleAddGear` in Dashboard.tsx:48-107)
- Creates a single gear object with user_id and all gear fields
- Uses `supabase.from('gear_items').insert(gearData).select()`
- Returns the created item and updates the gear count

## 2. **Bulk import** (`handleImportGear` in Dashboard.tsx:109-153)
- Maps an array of `ParsedGearItem` objects to database schema format
- Performs bulk insert using `supabase.from('gear_items').insert(gearItems).select()`
- All items inserted in a single database operation for efficiency
- Updates gear count by the number of imported items

Both methods use Supabase's `.insert()` method which automatically handles authentication via Row Level Security policies defined in the database migrations.

import { supabase } from './supabase'
import type { GearItem } from '@/types/database'

export interface CreateGearInput {
  user_id: string
  name: string
  weight_grams: number
  category: string
  quantity: number
  worn: boolean
  consumable: boolean
  notes?: string | null
  price?: number | null
  description?: string | null
  image_url?: string | null
  brand?: string | null
}

export interface UpdateGearInput {
  name?: string
  weight_grams?: number
  category?: string
  quantity?: number
  worn?: boolean
  consumable?: boolean
  notes?: string | null
  price?: number | null
  description?: string | null
  image_url?: string | null
  brand?: string | null
}

export const gearItems = {
  async create(item: CreateGearInput): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert(item)
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  },

  async createMany(items: CreateGearInput[]): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert(items)
      .select()

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  },

  async read(userId: string): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('user_id', userId)
      .order('category')
      .order('name')

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  },

  async readById(id: string, userId: string): Promise<GearItem | null> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', userId)
      .single()

    if (error) {
      if (error.code === 'PGRST116') return null
      throw error
    }
    return data
  },

  async update(id: string, userId: string, updates: UpdateGearInput): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .update(updates)
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', userId)
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  },

  async destroy(id: string, userId: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .delete()
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', userId)

    if (error) throw error
  },

  async destroyMany(ids: string[], userId: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .delete()
      .in('id', ids)
      .eq('user_id', userId)

    if (error) throw error
  }
}

import { supabase } from './supabase'
import type { GearItem } from '@/types/database'
import type { Repository } from './persistence'

class GearRepository implements Repository<GearItem> {
  private userId: string

  constructor(userId: string) {
    this.userId = userId
  }

  async create(item: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert({ ...item, user_id: this.userId })
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async read(id: string): Promise<GearItem | null> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .single()

    if (error && error.code !== 'PGRST116') throw error
    return data
  }

  async update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .update(updates)
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async delete(id: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .delete()
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)

    if (error) throw error
  }

  async list(): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .order('category')
      .order('name')

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }

  async createBulk(items: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const itemsWithUserId = items.map(item => ({ ...item, user_id: this.userId }))
    
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert(itemsWithUserId)
      .select()

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }
}

export const createGearRepository = (userId: string) => new GearRepository(userId)

import { supabase } from './supabase'
import type { GearItem } from '@/types/database'
import type { Repository } from './persistence'

class GearRepository implements Repository<GearItem> {
  private userId: string

  constructor(userId: string) {
    this.userId = userId
  }

  async create(item: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert({ ...item, user_id: this.userId })
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async read(id: string): Promise<GearItem | null> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .single()

    if (error && error.code !== 'PGRST116') throw error
    return data
  }

  async update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .update(updates)
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async delete(id: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .delete()
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)

    if (error) throw error
  }

  async list(): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .order('category')
      .order('name')

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }

  async createBulk(items: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const itemsWithUserId = items.map(item => ({ ...item, user_id: this.userId }))
    
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert(itemsWithUserId)
      .select()

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }
}

export const createGearRepository = (userId: string) => new GearRepository(userId)

content.text:
There are several documentation formats that work particularly well with agentic coding models like Claude Code:

## 1. **ADRs (Architecture Decision Records)**
Structured documents that capture the "why" behind decisions. Great for agents because they provide context and rationale.

```markdown
# ADR-001: Use Repository Pattern for Data Access

## Status
Accepted

## Context
We need a consistent way to access Supabase that can be easily mocked for testing.

## Decision
Implement a Repository pattern with a generic interface.

## Consequences
- ✅ Testable without hitting real database
- ✅ Consistent API across entities
- ⚠️ Additional abstraction layer
```

## 2. **CLAUDE.md / AI.md Files**
Project-specific instructions for AI agents. Already in your project! These are becoming a standard practice.

```markdown
# CLAUDE.md

## Commands
npm run dev  # Start development server

## Architecture Decisions
- Use Repository pattern for all database operations
- Store weights in grams for consistency
- Use Supabase RLS for security

## Code Style
- No comments unless requested
- Follow existing patterns
```

## 3. **Inline Decision Comments**
Strategic comments that explain non-obvious decisions:

```typescript
// Decision: Using createMany() instead of individual inserts
// for better performance with bulk imports (ADR-002)
await gearRepo.createMany(items)
```

## 4. **Living Documentation (Specs)**
Your project already uses this with `specs/` folder. These work well because agents can read and understand requirements:

```
specs/
├── mvp-technical-specification.md
├── delivery-plan.md
└── architecture-decisions/
    ├── ADR-001-persistence-layer.md
    └── ADR-002-bulk-operations.md
```

## 5. **Type-Driven Documentation**
Let types document the architecture:

```typescript
/**
 * Repository interface enforces consistent CRUD operations
 * See ADR-001 for rationale
 */
export interface Repository<T> {
  create(item: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<T>
  // ... other methods
}
```

## Best Practices for Agent-Friendly Docs:

1. **Be explicit about constraints**: "NEVER use raw SQL, ALWAYS use Repository"
2. **Include examples**: Agents learn patterns from examples
3. **Document the "why"**: Context helps agents make better decisions
4. **Keep it current**: Stale docs are worse than no docs
5. **Use structured formats**: Markdown headers, lists, and code blocks

Your CLAUDE.md is already following these practices well. Consider adding an `architecture-decisions/` folder for more complex decisions that need detailed documentation.

input.content:
# ADR-001: Repository Pattern for Persistence Layer

## Status
Accepted

## Date
2025-08-27

## Context
The application needs to interact with Supabase for data persistence. Initially, database operations were scattered throughout components (e.g., Dashboard component directly calling `supabase.from('gear_items')`), which created several issues:

- **Testing difficulty**: Components couldn't be tested without mocking Supabase internals
- **Code duplication**: Similar database queries were repeated across components  
- **Tight coupling**: Business logic was mixed with database access logic
- **User scoping**: Each query needed to remember to filter by `user_id`
- **No single source of truth**: Database operations were inconsistent

## Decision
Implement a Repository pattern with:

1. **Generic `Repository<T>` interface** defining standard CRUD operations
2. **Concrete implementations** (e.g., `GearRepository`) that handle entity-specific logic
3. **User scoping built-in** to prevent data leaks between users
4. **Bulk operations support** for efficient imports

### Interface Design
```typescript
export interface Repository<T> {
  create(item: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<T>
  createMany(items: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<T[]>
  read(id: string): Promise<T | null>
  update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<T>
  delete(id: string): Promise<void>
  list(): Promise<T[]>
  count(): Promise<number>
}
```

## Consequences

### Positive
- ✅ **Testable**: Repository can be easily mocked in tests
- ✅ **Consistent API**: All entities follow the same pattern
- ✅ **User isolation**: User scoping is centralized and automatic
- ✅ **Performance**: Bulk operations and count queries are optimized
- ✅ **Maintainable**: Database logic is in one place per entity
- ✅ **Type-safe**: Generic interface ensures type safety

### Negative
- ⚠️ **Additional abstraction**: One more layer between components and database
- ⚠️ **Learning curve**: Developers need to understand the pattern

### Neutral
- 🔄 Components now depend on repository instances rather than Supabase directly
- 🔄 Repository creation requires user ID at instantiation

## Implementation Notes

### Usage Example
```typescript
// In Dashboard component
const gearRepo = createGearRepository(user.id)
const count = await gearRepo.count()
const items = await gearRepo.list()
```

### Testing Example  
```typescript
// Mock the repository in tests
const mockRepo = {
  create: vi.fn(),
  list: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([mockItem1, mockItem2])
}
```

## References
- [Repository Pattern - Martin Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/repository.html)
- Original implementation: `/src/lib/persistence.ts`, `/src/lib/gearRepository.ts`
- Tests: `/src/lib/gearRepository.test.ts`

## Future Considerations
- Could add caching layer to repositories
- Might want to add pagination support to `list()` method
- Consider adding transaction support for complex operations
- May want to create a base repository class to reduce boilerplate

- ⚠️ **Additional abstraction**: One more layer between components and database
- ⚠️ **Learning curve**: Developers need to understand the pattern

### Neutral
- 🔄 Components now depend on repository instances rather than Supabase directly
- 🔄 Repository creation requires user ID at instantiation

## Implementation Notes

### Usage Example
```typescript
// In Dashboard component
const gearRepo = createGearRepository(user.id)
const count = await gearRepo.count()
const items = await gearRepo.list()
```

### Testing Example  
```typescript
// Mock the repository in tests
const mockRepo = {
  create: vi.fn(),
  list: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([mockItem1, mockItem2])
}
```

## References
- [Repository Pattern - Martin Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/repository.html)
- Original implementation: `/src/lib/persistence.ts`, `/src/lib/gearRepository.ts`
- Tests: `/src/lib/gearRepository.test.ts`

## Future Considerations
- Could add caching layer to repositories
- Might want to add pagination support to `list()` method
- Consider adding transaction support for complex operations
- May want to create a base repository class to reduce boilerplate

# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

This directory contains Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) that document important architectural decisions made in the BetterPack project.

## What is an ADR?

An ADR is a document that captures an important architectural decision made along with its context and consequences. ADRs help:
- Future developers understand why decisions were made
- AI coding assistants like Claude Code understand system design rationale  
- Teams avoid revisiting the same discussions
- Maintain consistency across the codebase

## ADR Format

Each ADR follows this structure:
- **Status**: Draft, Accepted, Deprecated, Superseded
- **Context**: What prompted this decision?
- **Decision**: What did we decide to do?
- **Consequences**: What are the positive, negative, and neutral outcomes?

## Current ADRs

| ADR | Title | Status | Date |
|-----|-------|--------|------|

1. Copy the template or follow the format of existing ADRs
2. Number it sequentially (ADR-002, ADR-003, etc.)
3. Include implementation examples when relevant
4. Reference related code files
5. Update this README with the new ADR

When working with this codebase, please:
- Read relevant ADRs to understand architectural decisions
- Follow patterns established in accepted ADRs
- Suggest new ADRs for significant architectural changes
- Reference ADR numbers in code comments when implementing decisions

The current `Repository<T>` interface design has a flaw when used with user-scoped entities like `GearItem`. The `create`, `createMany`, and `update` methods expect arguments that include the `user_id` property. However, the `GearRepository` is responsible for managing the `user_id` based on the user it was instantiated with.

This leads to two problems:
1.  **Confusing API**: The calling code (e.g., `Dashboard.tsx`) is required to pass a `user_id` that is then ignored and overwritten by the repository.
2.  **Potential Security Issue**: The `update` method signature allows attempting to change the `user_id` of an item, which should be prohibited.

A better design would be to ensure the types for creating and updating items do not include properties managed by the repository (like `user_id` in this case). +# ADR-001: Repository Pattern for Persistence Layer
+
+## Status
+Accepted
+
+## Date
+2025-08-27
+
+## Context
+The application needs to interact with Supabase for data persistence. Initially, database operations were scattered throughout components (e.g., Dashboard component directly calling `supabase.from('gear_items')`), which created several issues:
+
+- **Testing difficulty**: Components couldn't be tested without mocking Supabase internals
+- **Code duplication**: Similar database queries were repeated across components  
+- **Tight coupling**: Business logic was mixed with database access logic
+- **User scoping**: Each query needed to remember to filter by `user_id`
+- **No single source of truth**: Database operations were inconsistent
+
+## Decision
+Implement a Repository pattern with:
+
+1. **Generic `Repository<T>` interface** defining standard CRUD operations
+2. **Concrete implementations** (e.g., `GearRepository`) that handle entity-specific logic
+3. **User scoping built-in** to prevent data leaks between users
+4. **Bulk operations support** for efficient imports
+
+### Interface Design
+```typescript
+export interface Repository<T> {
+  create(item: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<T>
+  createMany(items: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<T[]>
+  read(id: string): Promise<T | null>
+  update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<T>
+  delete(id: string): Promise<void>
+  list(): Promise<T[]>
+  count(): Promise<number>
+}","path":"specs/adrs/ADR-001-repository-pattern-for-persistence.md","commit_id":"7b52b8bbd6202e334a629b0c3f68ba82482203f7","original_commit_id":"7b52b8bbd6202e334a629b0c3f68ba82482203f7","user":{"login":"gemini-code-assist[bot]","id":176961590,"node_id":"BOT_kgDOCow4Ng","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/in/956858?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D","html_url":"https://github.com/apps/gemini-code-assist","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/received_events","type":"Bot","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"body":"![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The current `Repository<T>` interface design has a flaw when used with user-scoped entities like `GearItem`. The `create`, `createMany`, and `update` methods expect arguments that include the `user_id` property. However, the `GearRepository` is responsible for managing the `user_id` based on the user it was instantiated with.

This leads to two problems:
1.  **Confusing API**: The calling code (e.g., `Dashboard.tsx`) is required to pass a `user_id` that is then ignored and overwritten by the repository.
2.  **Potential Security Issue**: The `update` method signature allows attempting to change the `user_id` of an item, which should be prohibited.

A better design would be to ensure the types for creating and updating items do not include properties managed by the repository (like `user_id` in this case). +# ADR-001: Repository Pattern for Persistence Layer
+
+## Status
+Accepted
+
+## Date
+2025-08-27
+
+## Context
+The application needs to interact with Supabase for data persistence. Initially, database operations were scattered throughout components (e.g., Dashboard component directly calling `supabase.from('gear_items')`), which created several issues:
+
+- **Testing difficulty**: Components couldn't be tested without mocking Supabase internals
+- **Code duplication**: Similar database queries were repeated across components  
+- **Tight coupling**: Business logic was mixed with database access logic
+- **User scoping**: Each query needed to remember to filter by `user_id`
+- **No single source of truth**: Database operations were inconsistent
+
+## Decision
+Implement a Repository pattern with:
+
+1. **Generic `Repository<T>` interface** defining standard CRUD operations
+2. **Concrete implementations** (e.g., `GearRepository`) that handle entity-specific logic
+3. **User scoping built-in** to prevent data leaks between users
+4. **Bulk operations support** for efficient imports
+

+  read(id: string): Promise<T | null>
+  update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<T>
+  delete(id: string): Promise<void>
+  list(): Promise<T[]>
+  count(): Promise<number>
+}","path":"specs/adrs/ADR-001-repository-pattern-for-persistence.md","commit_id":"7b52b8bbd6202e334a629b0c3f68ba82482203f7","original_commit_id":"7b52b8bbd6202e334a629b0c3f68ba82482203f7","user":{"login":"gemini-code-assist[bot]","id":176961590,"node_id":"BOT_kgDOCow4Ng","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/in/956858?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D","html_url":"https://github.com/apps/gemini-code-assist","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/gemini-code-assist%5Bbot%5D/received_events","type":"Bot","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"body":"![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

import { supabase } from './supabase'
import type { GearItem } from '@/types/database'
import type { Repository } from './persistence'

class GearRepository implements Repository<GearItem> {
  private userId: string

  constructor(userId: string) {
    this.userId = userId
  }

  async create(item: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert({ ...item, user_id: this.userId })
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async read(id: string): Promise<GearItem | null> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .single()

    if (error && error.code !== 'PGRST116') throw error
    return data
  }

  async update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .update(updates)
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async delete(id: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .delete()
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)

    if (error) throw error
  }

  async list(): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .order('category')
      .order('name')

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }

  async createMany(items: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const itemsWithUserId = items.map(item => ({ ...item, user_id: this.userId }))
    
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert(itemsWithUserId)
      .select()

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }

  async count(): Promise<number> {
    const { count, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)

    if (error) throw error
    return count || 0
  }
}

export const createGearRepository = (userId: string) => new GearRepository(userId)

import { supabase } from './supabase'
import type { GearItem } from '@/types/database'
import type { Repository } from './persistence'

class GearRepository implements Repository<GearItem> {
  private readonly userId: string

  constructor(userId: string) {
    this.userId = userId
  }

  async create(item: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert({ ...item, user_id: this.userId })
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async read(id: string): Promise<GearItem | null> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .single()

    if (error && error.code !== 'PGRST116') throw error
    return data
  }

  async update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<GearItem> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .update(updates)
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .select()
      .single()

    if (error) throw error
    return data
  }

  async delete(id: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .delete()
      .eq('id', id)
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)

    if (error) throw error
  }

  async list(): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*')
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)
      .order('category')
      .order('name')

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }

  async createMany(items: Omit<GearItem, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<GearItem[]> {
    const itemsWithUserId = items.map(item => ({ ...item, user_id: this.userId }))
    
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .insert(itemsWithUserId)
      .select()

    if (error) throw error
    return data || []
  }

  async count(): Promise<number> {
    const { count, error } = await supabase
      .from('gear_items')
      .select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })
      .eq('user_id', this.userId)

    if (error) throw error
    return count || 0
  }
}

export const createGearRepository = (userId: string) => new GearRepository(userId)

# ADR-001: Repository Pattern for Persistence Layer

## Status
Accepted

## Date
2025-08-27

## Context
The application needs to interact with Supabase for data persistence. Initially, database operations were scattered throughout components (e.g., Dashboard component directly calling `supabase.from('gear_items')`), which created several issues:

- **Testing difficulty**: Components couldn't be tested without mocking Supabase internals
- **Code duplication**: Similar database queries were repeated across components  
- **Tight coupling**: Business logic was mixed with database access logic
- **User scoping**: Each query needed to remember to filter by `user_id`
- **No single source of truth**: Database operations were inconsistent

## Decision
Implement a Repository pattern with:

1. **Generic `Repository<T>` interface** defining standard CRUD operations
2. **Concrete implementations** (e.g., `GearRepository`) that handle entity-specific logic
3. **User scoping built-in** to prevent data leaks between users
4. **Bulk operations support** for efficient imports

### Interface Design
```typescript
export interface Repository<T> {
  create(item: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>): Promise<T>
  createMany(items: Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>[]): Promise<T[]>
  read(id: string): Promise<T | null>
  update(id: string, updates: Partial<Omit<T, 'id' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at'>>): Promise<T>
  delete(id: string): Promise<void>
  list(): Promise<T[]>
  count(): Promise<number>
}
```

## Consequences

### Positive
- ✅ **Testable**: Repository can be easily mocked in tests
- ✅ **Consistent API**: All entities follow the same pattern
- ✅ **User isolation**: User scoping is centralized and automatic
- ✅ **Performance**: Bulk operations and count queries are optimized
- ✅ **Maintainable**: Database logic is in one place per entity
- ✅ **Type-safe**: Generic interface ensures type safety

### Negative
- ⚠️ **Additional abstraction**: One more layer between components and database
- ⚠️ **Learning curve**: Developers need to understand the pattern

### Neutral
- 🔄 Components now depend on repository instances rather than Supabase directly
- 🔄 Repository creation requires user ID at instantiation

## Implementation Notes

### Usage Example
```typescript
// In Dashboard component
const gearRepo = createGearRepository(user.id)
const count = await gearRepo.count()
const items = await gearRepo.list()
```

### Testing Example  
```typescript
// Mock the repository in tests
const mockRepo = {
  create: vi.fn(),
  list: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([mockItem1, mockItem2])
}
```

## References
- [Repository Pattern - Martin Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/repository.html)
- Original implementation: `/src/lib/persistence.ts`, `/src/lib/gearRepository.ts`
- Tests: `/src/lib/gearRepository.test.ts`

## Future Considerations
- Could add caching layer to repositories
- Might want to add pagination support to `list()` method
- Consider adding transaction support for complex operations
- May want to create a base repository class to reduce boilerplate

input.plan:
# Mobile Experience Improvement Plan

Based on my analysis of the current BetterPack application, here's a comprehensive plan to significantly improve the mobile experience:

## Current Issues Identified

1. **Typography & Spacing**: Large text sizes (text-3xl) and generous spacing aren't optimized for mobile screens
2. **Navigation**: Header becomes cramped on mobile with hidden elements (email, "Sign out" text)  
3. **Cards & Layout**: Stats cards use 4-column grid that may not flow well on mobile
4. **Touch Targets**: Some buttons and interactive elements may be too small for touch
5. **Forms**: Import and add gear forms likely need mobile-specific optimizations
6. **Content Hierarchy**: Welcome messaging takes up valuable mobile screen real estate

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Mobile-First Header & Navigation
- Replace cramped header with mobile-optimized version
- Add hamburger menu for mobile navigation
- Implement proper mobile touch targets (min 44px)
- Show user avatar instead of full email on mobile

### Phase 2: Responsive Dashboard Layout  
- Implement mobile-first card grid (1 column on mobile, responsive breakpoints)
- Optimize typography scale for mobile (smaller headings, better line heights)
- Reduce padding/margins for mobile to maximize content space
- Add mobile-specific stats card layout

### Phase 3: Mobile-Optimized Forms
- Make AddGearForm mobile-friendly with better input spacing
- Optimize ImportGearForm for mobile workflows
- Add mobile-specific form validation and feedback
- Implement mobile-friendly file upload for CSV imports

### Phase 4: Touch & Interaction Improvements
- Ensure all buttons meet minimum touch target size (44px)
- Add touch-friendly hover states and transitions
- Implement swipe gestures where appropriate
- Add mobile-specific loading states

### Phase 5: Mobile-Specific Features
- Add pull-to-refresh functionality
- Implement mobile-friendly modals and dialogs  
- Add mobile share capabilities
- Optimize for mobile performance (lazy loading, etc.)

### Phase 6: Progressive Web App (PWA) Features
- Add service worker for offline functionality
- Implement app manifest for "Add to Home Screen"
- Add mobile-specific app icons
- Enable mobile push notifications (future)

## Technical Approach

- Use Tailwind's mobile-first responsive design principles
- Implement proper breakpoints: `sm:` (640px+), `md:` (768px+), `lg:` (1024px+)
- Add touch-specific CSS utilities and components
- Create mobile-specific component variants where needed
- Use CSS Grid and Flexbox for optimal mobile layouts

## Success Metrics

- Improved mobile usability scores
- Faster mobile interaction times
- Better mobile conversion rates for gear entry
- Positive user feedback on mobile experience

This plan will transform BetterPack into a mobile-first application that works seamlessly across all devices, with particular attention to the unique needs of mobile users managing their outdoor gear.

CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card' import { Mountain, Package, MapPin, Weight, Plus, LogOut, User, X, Upload, FileText, Menu } from 'lucide-react' import { AddGearForm } from '@/components/gear/AddGearForm' import { ImportGearForm } from '@/components/gear/ImportGearForm' import { createGearRepository } from '@/lib/gearRepository' import { captureError } from '@/lib/sentry' import { toast } from '@/hooks/useToast' import type { ParsedGearItem } from '@/utils/csvParser' export function Dashboard() { const { user, signOut } = useAuth() const [showAddGear, setShowAddGear] = useState(false) const [showImport, setShowImport] = useState(false) const [showMobileMenu, setShowMobileMenu] = useState(false) const [gearCount, setGearCount] = useState(0) // Fetch initial gear count on component mount useEffect(() => { const fetchGearCount = async () => { if (!user) return try { const gearRepo = createGearRepository(user.id) const count = await gearRepo.count() setGearCount(count) } catch (error) { captureError(error as Error, { component: 'Dashboard', action: 'fetchGearCount' }) // Don't show error toast on initial load console.error('Failed to load gear count:', error) } } fetchGearCount() }, [user]) const handleAddGear = async (gear: { name: string weight_grams: number category: string quantity: number worn: boolean consumable: boolean notes?: string | null price?: number | null description?: string | null image_url?: string | null brand?: string | null }) => { if (!user) return try { const gearRepo = createGearRepository(user.id) await gearRepo.create({ name: gear.name, weight_grams: gear.weight_grams, category: gear.category, quantity: gear.quantity, worn: gear.worn, consumable: gear.consumable, notes: gear.notes || null, price: gear.price || null, description: gear.description || null, image_url: gear.image_url || null, brand: gear.brand || null }) // Update gear count setGearCount(prev => prev + 1) // Close the form setShowAddGear(false) // Show success toast with item name const itemName = gear.brand ? `${gear.brand} ${gear.name}` : gear.name toast.success(`✓ ${itemName} added to your gear library`) } catch (error) { captureError(error as Error, { component: 'Dashboard', action: 'handleAddGear' }) console.error('Error adding gear:', error) toast.error('Failed to add gear', 'Please try again or check your connection.') } } const handleImportGear = async (items: ParsedGearItem[]) => { if (!user) return try { const gearRepo = createGearRepository(user.id) // Transform ParsedGearItem to match our database schema const gearItems = items.map(item => ({ name: item.name, brand: item.brand || null, weight_grams: item.weight_grams, category: item.category, quantity: item.quantity, worn: item.worn, consumable: item.consumable, price: item.price || null, notes: item.notes || null, description: item.description || null, image_url: null })) // Bulk insert all items await gearRepo.createMany(gearItems) // Update gear count setGearCount(prevCount => prevCount + items.length) // Close import form setShowImport(false) // Show success message toast.success( `Successfully imported ${items.length} items!`, 'Your gear has been added to your library.' ) // Refresh the page data if needed // You might want to trigger a re-fetch of gear items here } catch (error) { captureError(error as Error, { component: 'Dashboard', action: 'importGear', metadata: { itemCount: items.length } }) console.error('Error importing gear:', error) toast.error('Failed to import gear', 'Please try again or import fewer items at once.') } } return (
